name: JW Marriott Chicago
positioning: Luxury hotel in a 1914 Daniel Burnham-designed former bank in the heart of Chicago's Loop, with Pullman railcar-inspired rooms and the Spa at JW Chicago
best_for: Travelers who want a historic architectural landmark as their base in the Loop
Guests who want a spa with a steam room, infrared sauna and Hammam chambers in the city

facts.text: The hotel occupies a historic 1914 building designed by Daniel Burnham.
The building is the former Continental and Commercial Bank.
The hotel is in the heart of Chicago's Loop.
The hotel is near Union Station, the Art Institute of Chicago and Millennium Park.
Guest rooms have 9-foot ceilings and crown molding.
Suites have a separate living area and an expansive master bath.
The full-service spa offers massages, facials, body treatments and a nail salon.
The hotel has an indoor swimming pool and whirlpool.
Group fitness classes are led by professional trainers.
Henrietta is a Tuscan-inspired modern Italian restaurant on the hotel's second floor.
The hotel's event venues include the Burnham Ballroom.

highlights.text: The hotel is set in a 1914 Daniel Burnham-designed building that was once the Continental and Commercial Bank.
Rooms and suites are inspired by Pullman's luxury railcars.
The Spa at JW Chicago has a steam room, an infrared sauna and two Hammam chambers.
Bathrooms have a soaking tub, a separate shower and dual vanity sinks.

considerations.text: Pets are not allowed at the hotel.
Parking is by valet, with independent off-site parking across the street.
WhataHotel notes a busy downtown setting that may feel less relaxing than a secluded retreat.
